Subject: Request for subprocessor inventory + evidence pack

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our vendor onboarding checklist we need: the full subprocessor inventory (names, purpose, location, subprocessors that access production data), your SOC 2 report or equivalent, and any dataflow artifacts for storage/KMS usage. Our deadline for a first pass is next Tuesday (2026-12-01).

Can you confirm what you can provide by then and whether you’ll need any NDAs or redactions? Also list any subprocessors that have logical access to customer data (e.g., logging, analytics, backups).

Best,
Maya Alvarez
Procurement Manager, HealthCore Labs

Subject: Re: Request for subprocessor inventory + evidence pack

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. We can deliver a scoped assurance kit by 2026-12-01. Plan below: 

1) Deliverable 1 (by 2026-12-01): redacted_subprocessor_inventory.csv — includes vendor name, function, hosting region, minimal contact, and whether they have production data access. We will redact internal contact emails and employee names.
2) Deliverable 2 (by 2026-12-01): redacted_SOC2_report_2026.pdf — redacted SOC 2 Type II report (redaction limited to internal audit IDs and non-customer-facing operational metrics).
3) Deliverable 3 (by 2026-12-02): subproc_dataflow_diagram_v1.png and an architecture note explaining KMS flows and backup retention.

Questions for you: does HealthCore require vendor-level KMS key provenance (e.g., which vendors are in the same KMS tenant) or is confirmation that Redwood exclusively manages CMKs sufficient? Also, do you need evidence of contractual data processing clauses for all subprocessors or only for those with production-data access?

I’m CCing Markus (security leads for supply-chain) and Marissa (privacy/compliance) to confirm the redaction scope.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Strategic Partnerships — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request for subprocessor inventory + evidence pack

Hi all — quick notes from security:

- We will include the SOC 2 Type II with redactions as Vanessa outlined. The redacted_SOC2_report_2026.pdf will include the control narratives and scope plus a signed auditor cover page.
- For KMS: Redwood manages customer CMKs in our KMS and we support customer-managed keys for Private deployments. For hosted accounts, CMKs are in our tenant; we will provide a key lineage statement (not raw key material). If HealthCore needs tenant mapping to subprocessor storage systems (e.g., which vendor buckets are encrypted under which tenant key), we can provide a table for subprocessors that have storage access.
- CloudStor is a storage partner that holds encrypted backups; they have access to encrypted objects but not to decrypted keys. Per your ask, we’ll mark CloudStor as a subprocessor with logical backup access and include contractual DPA references.

Attached: preliminary redacted_SOC2_report_2026.pdf (redacted), redacted_subprocessor_inventory.csv (first pass). We’ll follow with a dataflow PNG and a short narrative.

Action items: Vanessa to push the Drive folder and we’ll notify you when the evidence drop is ready.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Director, Applied Security — Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwoodinference.com

Thanks — quick follow-ups from our security team after reviewing the initial inventory: 

1) CloudStor: please include the subcontractor contact (either an audit or security liaison) and the most recent evidence of encryption-at-rest configs and backup retention policy.
2) KMS lineage: we need a mapping between storage buckets and the KMS tenant (can be redacted to tenant IDs).
3) Data flows: is there a single place we can review the flow from customer ingestion -> realtime inference -> logging/analytics -> backups? A single annotated diagram is preferred.

If possible, please upload the artifacts to the Drive link Vanessa referenced and mark files that contain sensitive internal identifiers as "REDACTED" in the filename. We will triage and circle back with any follow ups.

Thanks,
Autumn Li
Security Engineer — HealthCore Labs
security@healthcore.com
